final_answer:
>>> The probability of getting exactly k successes (in this case, heads) in n independent trials (coin flips) with a success probability of p on each trial is given by the binomial probability formula: P(k) = C(n, k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k).

>>> In this scenario, n = 10 (number of coin flips), k = 7 (number of heads), and p = 0.5 (probability of getting heads on a single flip, since the coin is fair).

>>> To calculate the combination C(10, 7), which represents the number of ways to choose 7 successes (heads) out of 10 trials, we use the formula C(n, k) = n! / (k! * (n-k)!). For C(10, 7), this becomes 10! / (7! * 3!) = (10 * 9 * 8) / (3 * 2 * 1) = 120.

>>> Next, compute p^k = 0.5^7 = 1/128 ≈ 0.0078125 and (1-p)^(n-k) = 0.5^(10-7) = 0.5^3 = 1/8 = 0.125.

>>> Multiplying all components together: P(7) = C(10, 7) * p^7 * (1-p)^3 = 120 * 0.0078125 * 0.125 = 120 * 0.0009765625 ≈ 0.1171875.

>>> The probability of getting exactly 7 heads in 10 flips of a fair coin is approximately 0.1172 or 11.72%. This means that in about 11.72% of such experiments, one would expect to see exactly 7 heads.
